To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the configuration of personal software systems can be achieved using a goal model, in which the goals of the users are matched with system functionality.

(1) the configuration options of a typical e-mail system reflect the ways with which user goals can be achieved, and (2) the goal model can be used as a means for reasoning about the configuration process, facilitating thereby the automatic configuration of the e-mail system by reasoning about its goal model.

the personalization of common personal software can be achieved by matching high level user goals with system configurations, and that this matching is facilitated by the existence of a goal model that describes the ways with which each goal can be achieved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automatic generation of personalized configurations of common personal software.

the following questions: (1) How to configure personal software systems in a requirements-driven way? (2) Can we automate this process? (3) How to ensure consistency and meaningfulness of the configuration result?
the development of a methodology for the configuration of personal software systems, and with the implementation of the proposed methodology as an automatic configuration tool.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the goal model is a powerful tool for configuring personal software systems.

the configuration of common personal systems should be based on a goal model that is constructed from the requirements of the user, and that the user's goals should be used as a basis for reasoning about system configurations, thus facilitating personalization.
the goal-based approach to configuration is the most promising one.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a requirements-driven approach to personalizing the common personal software.
the configuration process is a goal-driven process, and that a requirements-driven approach is more appropriate to be applied in order to configure personal software.
we propose an approach that enables the automatic personalization of common personal software by reasoning about user goals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the configuration of common personal software is not a trivial task, and should be supported in a way that is meaningful to the users.

the goal model can be used for automatic configuration of the e-mail client, and that the configuration process is not a mere trial-and-error process, but a process that is guided by a model of the user goals and the system functionality.
the personalization of software systems can be facilitated by a requirements-driven approach.
